pages.ja:
傷を負った体は、深い眠りを欲している。
だが心は未だあの光景の中にいて、泥のような眠りには至らない。
治りきらない体は熱く、悔やみきれない心は燻ったままだ。

pages.en:
My wounded body longs for deep sleep.

But my heart remains trapped in that scene, unable to sink into sleep as deep and senseless as mud.

My half-healed body burns with fever, while regret continues to smolder in my heart.
pages.mirrorMoon:
My injured body wants to sleep
deeply to get as much rest as it can.
deeply.
But my mind is still buried in that scene, and I can’t fall into a deep sleep.
My still-injured body is burning, and my mind that cannot mourn enough is still burning too.

pages.en:
Am I having a nightmare?

Half-conscious in the shallows of sleep, I dream.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I might be having a nightmare.
As I doze, I see a dream in my unclear mind.

pages.ja:
……どれだけの人間が犠牲になったのか。
死傷者はいないと遠坂は言っていたが、それは表面だけの話だ。
強引に命を吸い出すような真似をされて、後遺症が出ない筈がない。
長期に渡る身体不良、酸欠による記憶障害。
肌に重傷を負った生徒もいた。
その傷痕は、たとえ完治しようと一生涯残るものだ。

pages.en:
…How many people fell victim to it?

Tohsaka said there were no casualties, but that is only true on the surface.

There is no way anyone could have their life forcibly drained without suffering lasting effects.

Chronic illness. Memory damage from lack of oxygen.

Some students suffered terrible injuries to their skin.

Even if those wounds heal completely, the scars will remain for the rest of their lives.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…How many victims were there?
Tohsaka said nobody died, but that is only from the outside.
Having had their life sucked out by force, there will certainly be after-effects.
Long-term physical disabilities and mental damage from lack of oxygen.
There were even students that had
their skin melted.
serious injuries.
That scar is something that will stay with them for the rest of their lives even if it heals.

……体が痛む。
殺されかけた
否、間違いなく死んでいた体が痙攣する。
巻き込まれたみんなも災難だったが、それでもおまえはよくやった。
本来なら死に至る傷と引き替えに災害を止められたのだ。
なら悔やむ事も恥じる事もない。
大人しく今は眠りに落ちてしまえ、とその痛みが訴えている。

pages.en:
…My body hurts.

The body that was nearly killed—no, that unquestionably died—trembles in pain.

Everyone caught in the disaster suffered, but even so, you did well.

You stopped the catastrophe in exchange for wounds that should have killed you.

You have nothing to regret. Nothing to be ashamed of.

Be still now, the pain urges me. Let yourself fall asleep.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…My body hurts.
My almost deadno, my absolutely dead body convulses.
It was unfortunate for everyone involved, but you still did well.
You were able to stop the disaster in exchange for a wound you would normally die from.
So there is nothing to mourn or to be ashamed of.
The pain tells me to quietly fall asleep for now.

pages.en:
No.

I cannot hide from it behind an excuse like that.
pages.mirrorMoon:
No.
I can’t deceive myself with such reasoning.

惨劇は起きて、自分はそこに居合わせて、何も出来なかった事に変わりはない。
俺は命を救ったというが。
同時に、誰一人として助けられなかった。
いっそアレが何かの間違いで、無かった事になるのなら
心も大人しく眠ってくれるだろうに。

pages.en:
The atrocity happened. I was there. And nothing changes the fact that I could do nothing.

They say I saved their lives.

But at the same time, I failed to save a single one of them.

If only it had all been some mistake—if only it could be made never to have happened—then perhaps my heart would consent to sleep.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It makes no difference to the fact that the disaster occurred while I was there, but I couldn’t do anything.
I say I saved lives, but…
…At the same time, I couldn’t save anybody.
If that was just a mistake, if it had never happenedI bet my mind and my body could go to sleep peacefully.

pages.ja:
……頭にきた。
体が弱って、心までそんな世迷い事をクチにするなんて、ふざけてる。
pages.jaRuby:
……頭にきた。

pages.en:
…That makes me angry.

My body grows weak, and now even my heart starts mouthing such nonsense.

What a joke.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I’m pissed off.
It’s ridiculous for my mind to grumble about such a thing.

pages.ja: そんな奇蹟はない。
pages.jaRuby: そんな奇蹟はない。
pages.en: No miracle like that exists.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There are no miracles like that.
There are no miracles like that.

pages.ja:
都合の悪い事だから、目の当てられない惨状だったから、その前に戻ってやり直せればなんて、ひどい侮辱だ。
起きてしまった事を『無かった事』になど出来ない。
それは不可能な事だし、それ以前に、やってはいけない事ではないのか。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Because the truth is inconvenient. Because the devastation is too awful to look upon. To wish I could return to before it happened and begin again would be a terrible insult.

What has happened cannot be made never to have happened.

It is impossible—and before that, surely it is something no one should ever do.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s a great insult to want to go back and redo things, just because I think they’re inconvenient and disastrous.
It’s impossible to take something that has already happened and make it so that it “didn’t happen”.
It’s impossible, and more importantly, it shouldn’t be done.

pages.ja:
……だから、あの出来事を無かった事になんて出来ない。
俺に出来る事はただ一つ
今も見続けているこの光景を憎むなら、二度と起こさせないように行動するだけだ。

pages.en:
…So I cannot erase what happened.

There is only one thing I can do. If I hate the scene that still fills my eyes, I must act to ensure it never happens again.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…That’s why I can’t pretend the event didn’t happen.
There’s only one thing I can doif I hate the scene I still see even now. I should just act to prevent it from ever happening again.

I open my eyes.

I draw a deep breath, filling my lungs with air.

I take a deep breath and draw air into my lungs.

pages.ja:
「
はあ」
冷たい冬の大気は、眠気と不安を削ぎ落としてくれた。
習慣というのは大したもので、時刻はまだ六時になったばかりだ。
起床の時間にきっかり目を覚ますあたり、体はわりと回復しているのではなかろうか。

pages.en:
“——Hah.”

The cold winter air strips away my drowsiness and unease.

Habit is a remarkable thing. It has only just turned six.

Waking at precisely my usual hour must mean my body has recovered fairly well.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Phew.”
The cold winter air takes away my drowsiness and uneasiness.
Habit is a great thing. It’s only a bit past six o’clock.
Maybe my body has healed quite well already as I’m awake at my usual time.

よし」
体を起こして布団を畳む。
そんな何でもない作業の途中、びしり、と。
亀裂でも入ったかのように、左肩が痛んだ。

I sit up and fold the futon.

In the midst of that utterly ordinary task, something cracks.

A sharp pain splits my left shoulder, as though a crack has opened through it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“All right.”
I get up and fold up the futon.
During that normal action…
A sharp pain runs through my left arm as if there’s a crack in my bone.

pages.ja:
「っ……まあ、そりゃそうだよな。さすがにまだ治りきってないか」
それでもあるのは『痛み』だけだ。
何日か前、バーサーカーに腹を斬られた時に比べれば幾分ましだろう。
あの時は体中がドロドロで、痛みより吐き気の方が酷かったんだから。

pages.en:
“Gh… Well, of course. I suppose it hasn't healed completely yet.”

Still, it is only pain.

Compared with a few days ago, when Berserker slashed open my stomach, this is considerably better.

Back then my whole body felt like sludge, and the nausea was worse than the pain.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…! Well, of course. There’s no way it would be healed already.”
But all that’s left is this pain.
It’s much better than when I got my stomach slashed by Berserker a few days ago.
At that time, my body was so weak that the nausea was worse than the pain.

陽射しは陰鬱として、力強さがなかった。
天気は一雨きそうなほど曇っている。

pages.en:
I step into the hall.

The sunlight is dull and listless.

Clouds heavy enough to promise rain cover the sky.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I go out into the hallway.
The sunlight is gloomy and offers no energy.
The weather is very cloudy like it’s going to rain.

「ああ、いま目が覚めた。そういうセイバーこそ今朝は早いんだな。いつもならまだ眠ってる時間じゃないか」
うん、朝飯が出来てもいないのに、セイバーが起きているのは珍しい。

“Shirou, you are awake…?”

“Yeah, I just woke up. You're up early yourself, Saber. Aren't you usually still asleep at this hour?”

It is unusual to see Saber awake before breakfast is even ready.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Shirou, you have awakened…?”
“Yeah, I just woke up. You’re up early today. You’re usually asleep at this time.”
Yeah, it’s unusual for Saber to be awake before breakfast is ready.

「……シロウ。私とて好きで眠っている訳ではありません。私が朝食まで眠っているのは、単に魔力を温存する為だと言った筈です。
その、いかにも普段から寝過ごしている、という物言いは止めてほしい」

pages.en:
“…Shirou. It is not as though I sleep because I enjoy it. I believe I told you that I remain asleep until breakfast merely to conserve magical energy.

“I would prefer that you not speak as though I habitually oversleep.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Shirou. I am not sleeping because I want to. I think I have told you already that I am sleeping until breakfast to save my magical energy.
Um, I wish you would not make it sound like I am always sleeping in.”

pages.ja:
「？ なんでさ。別にそんなつもりで言ってないぞ、俺。
単にこんな早起きしていいのかって思っただけだ」
「……ほう、そうですか。私が早起きするのはおかしい、と」
pages.jaRuby:
「？ なんでさ。別にそんなつもりで言ってないぞ、俺。

「……ほう、そうですか。私が早起きするのはおかしい、と」
pages.en:
“Huh? Why? I didn't mean it that way.

“I was only wondering whether you should be up this early.”

“…I see. So you find it strange for me to rise early.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…? Why? I didn’t intend to make it sound like that.
I was just wondering if it was okay for you to wake up this early.”
“…Oh, I see. So you are saying it is strange for me to wake up early?”

pages.ja:
セイバーはやけにつんけんとした物言いをする。
……気のせいだろうか。
今朝のセイバーはどこか、いつもより厳しいというか、遠慮がないように見えた。
pages.jaRuby:
セイバーはやけにつんけんとした物言いをする。

今朝のセイバーはどこか、いつもより厳しいというか、遠慮がないように見えた。
pages.en:
Saber's reply is unusually prickly.

…Or am I imagining it?

This morning she seems sterner than usual—or perhaps simply less reserved.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Saber sounds cranky.
…Is it just me?
It seems Saber is stricter today, or should I say she’s unreserved?

pages.ja:
「いや、おかしいとかじゃなくて、いいのかなって。
セイバーが頻繁に眠らなくちゃいけないのは俺のせいだ。だから今朝もできる限り眠っていないといけないんじゃないのか」
pages.jaRuby:

“I don't mean it's strange. I mean, is it all right?

“It's my fault you need to sleep so often in the first place. Shouldn't you rest as long as you can this morning too?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“No, not strange, but I’m wondering if it’s all right.
It’s my fault that you have to sleep a lot, right?
So
I know that, so
shouldn’t you be sleeping as long as you possibly can?”

pages.ja: 「当然です。ですが、それはあくまで待機状態にすぎません。私が眠っていたのは緊急時に備えてのもの。今の状態で眠るのは道理にかなわないではないですか」

pages.en: “Ordinarily, yes. But that is merely a state of waiting. I slept in order to remain prepared for an emergency. Under our present circumstances, continuing to sleep would make no sense.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Of course. But that is only when I am on standby. I was sleeping in anticipation of an emergency. I do not think it is logical for me to sleep in this situation.”

pages.ja:
「？ 道理にかなわないって、なんで。別に今は誰とも戦ってないし、襲われてもいないぞ」
「え……いえ、ですから、それは」
何か言いにくい事でもあるのか、セイバーは言葉を濁す。
pages.jaRuby:

“? Why wouldn't it? We're not fighting anyone right now, and no one is attacking us.”

“Ah… No, what I mean is…”

Perhaps there is something she finds difficult to say. Saber trails off.

“…? Why isn’t it logical? We’re not fighting anyone, nor is anyone attacking us right now.”
“Eh… no, I mean, that is…”
Saber is unclear as if there’s something she doesn’t want to say.

original.en:
The arrow of light that ravaged the corridor.

A wave of destruction that would have scattered my body without leaving so much as a speck of dust if Saber had not knocked me down.

If that was Rider's trump card, then however unimpressive her own abilities may be, we cannot afford to underestimate her.

No—far from taking her lightly, I have the feeling she may be an opponent we must not challenge at all.

pages.mirrorMoon: “So, Saber. You should have been able to tell what Rider’s Noble Phantasm was, right? You should have some idea since it was used right in front of you.”

pages.mirrorMoon:

If I had worried about such a thing, we would have been engulfed by it.”

pages.jaRuby: 「巻き込まれてたって……なに、ライダーの宝具って飛び道具なの？」

pages.mirrorMoon: “Engulfed… what, is Rider’s Noble Phantasm a projectile weapon?”

pages.ja: 「それに近いモノでした。分類的には凛の使う魔術に近い。アレは私の剣やランサーの槍のような、対人宝具ではないのでしょう」
pages.jaRuby: 「それに近いモノでした。分類的には凛の使う魔術に近い。アレは私の剣やランサーの槍のような、対人宝具ではないのでしょう」
pages.en: “It was something of that nature. In classification, it more closely resembled the magecraft you employ. It was likely not an Anti-Unit Noble Phantasm like my sword or Lancer's spear.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “It was something close to it. Its classification is close to the magic you use. It could not have been an anti-personnel Noble Phantasm, like my sword or Lancer’s lance.”

pages.ja:
「わたしの魔術に近いって、それこそ変よ。
セイバーの対魔術は神業じゃない。現代の魔術じゃまず貴女に傷を負わせる事はできない。その貴女が躱さなくちゃいけない魔術なんて、それは」

「わたしの魔術に近いって、それこそ変よ。

pages.en:
“Like my magecraft? That makes even less sense.

“Your Magic Resistance is nothing short of miraculous. Modern magecraft could hardly put a scratch on you. If it was magecraft powerful enough that even you had to evade it, then——”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s even stranger if it’s like my magic.
Your magic resistance is godly. No magic in the present day can hurt you. If there is a magic even you have to avoid, that would be…”

pages.ja:
「
はい。神秘はより強い神秘の前に無効化される。
私の鎧を通る事ができる神秘は、貴女たちの言う“魔法”か、神域に棲む幻想種だけです」

pages.en:
“——Yes. A Mystery is nullified in the presence of a greater Mystery.

“Only what you call Magic, or a Phantasmal Beast belonging to the divine realm, could penetrate my armor.”

“A Magician——are you saying Rider is a mage, Saber…!?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes. Divine mysteries are nullified by even stronger ones.
A divine mystery that can strike through my armor is what you people call ‘sorcery’ or a fantastic race with divinity.”
“Sorceryare you saying Rider is a magus…!?”

pages.ja:
「いえ、それほどの魔力は感じませんでした。
彼女はライダーです。魔法使いがいるとすれば、それはキャスターだけでしょう。ライダーの宝具は、おそらく別のモノだと思います」
pages.jaRuby:
「いえ、それほどの魔力は感じませんでした。

pages.en:
“No. I sensed no magical energy of such magnitude from her.

“She is Rider. If any Servant were a Magician, it would be Caster alone. I believe Rider's Noble Phantasm was something else.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“No, I did not feel so much magical energy from her.
She is of class Rider. If there is a magus, it could only be Caster. I believe Rider’s Noble Phantasm is something else.”

pages.ja:
セイバーの答えに、ほっと胸をなで下ろす遠坂。
が、こっちはいまいち話が掴めない。
pages.jaRuby:
セイバーの答えに、ほっと胸をなで下ろす遠坂。

Tohsaka sighs with relief at Saber's answer.

I, on the other hand, have not quite followed the conversation.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka gives a relieved sigh at Saber’s answer.
But I don’t quite get it.

pages.ja: 「セイバー。おまえの鎧っていうのはそんなに硬いものなのか？ 魔法でなければ通らない、なんて言うけど、それならランサーのゲイボルクは魔法って事になるが」
pages.jaRuby: 「セイバー。おまえの鎧っていうのはそんなに硬いものなのか？ 魔法でなければ通らない、なんて言うけど、それならランサーのゲイボルクは魔法って事になるが」
pages.en: “Saber. Is your armor really that strong? You say nothing short of Magic can get through it, but if that's true, then Lancer's Gae Bolg would have to be Magic.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Saber. Is your armor that strong? If you say only sorcery can go through it, then that would make Lancer’s Gae Bolg a sorcery as well.”

pages.ja: 「え……？ ええ、確かにランサーのゲイボルクは魔法に近い“呪い”ですが……凛、シロウに説明してあげてくれますか」
pages.jaRuby: 「え……？ ええ、確かにランサーのゲイボルクは魔法に近い“呪い”ですが……凛、シロウに説明してあげてくれますか」
pages.en: “What…? Yes, Gae Bolg's curse certainly approaches the realm of Magic, but… Rin, would you explain it to Shirou?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Eh…? Yes, Lancer’s Gae Bolg is certainly a ‘curse’ close to sorcery, but… Rin, could you please explain to Shirou?”

pages.ja: 「わたし？ ……まあいいけど。ようするに士郎はセイバーは魔法じゃないと傷つかない、と勘違いしてるわけね？」
pages.jaRuby: 「わたし？ ……まあいいけど。ようするに士郎はセイバーは魔法じゃないと傷つかない、と勘違いしてるわけね？」
pages.en: “Me? …Fine. In other words, Shirou has misunderstood you to mean that nothing short of Magic can hurt you. Is that right?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Me? …Well, okay. So in short, you are misinterpreting that Saber can be only hurt using sorcery, right?”

pages.ja:
「あ、いや……別にそういう訳じゃないけど。
ただ、そんなに頑丈な鎧なら凄いなって思っただけだ」
pages.jaRuby:
「あ、いや……別にそういう訳じゃないけど。
ただ、そんなに頑丈な鎧なら凄いなって思っただけだ」
pages.en:
“Oh, no… That isn't exactly what I meant.

“I just thought armor that durable sounded incredible.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Uh, no… that’s not exactly what I meant.
I just thought it was amazing if the armor is that strong.”

pages.ja: 「そりゃ凄いわよ。セイバーに限らず、サーヴァントってのはみんな英霊なのよ？ 霊体って事もあるけど、まっとうな手段じゃ傷一つつけられない。サーヴァントはそれ自体が神秘だから」
pages.jaRuby: 「そりゃ凄いわよ。セイバーに限らず、サーヴァントってのはみんな英霊なのよ？ 霊体って事もあるけど、まっとうな手段じゃ傷一つつけられない。サーヴァントはそれ自体が神秘だから」
pages.en: “Of course it's incredible. Not only Saber, but every Servant is a Heroic Spirit. Partly because they're spiritual beings, but ordinary means can't so much as scratch them. A Servant is itself a Mystery.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Of course it’s amazing. Not just Saber, but all the Servants are heroic spirits. There’s the fact that they’re spirits, but they can’t be hurt by normal means. That’s because Servants themselves are divine mysteries.”

pages.ja: 「物理的な手段でサーヴァントを傷つけられるのは、同じ英霊であるサーヴァントだけ。逆に言えばサーヴァント同士なら、ただのペーパーナイフでもセイバーを傷つける事はできる」
pages.jaRuby: 「物理的な手段でサーヴァントを傷つけられるのは、同じ英霊であるサーヴァントだけ。逆に言えばサーヴァント同士なら、ただのペーパーナイフでもセイバーを傷つける事はできる」
pages.en: “The only beings capable of physically harming a Servant are other Servants—other Heroic Spirits. Turn that around, and it means that between Servants, even an ordinary paper knife could wound Saber.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “The only ones that can physically hurt the Servants are other Servants, heroic spirits like them. So in other words, if a Servant was using it, even a paper knife could hurt Saber.”

pages.ja: 「……相手がサーヴァントなら、セイバーの鎧もそう鉄壁って訳じゃない……ってコトか？」
pages.jaRuby: 「……相手がサーヴァントなら、セイバーの鎧もそう鉄壁って訳じゃない……ってコトか？」
pages.en: “…So if her opponent is another Servant, Saber's armor isn't completely impenetrable after all?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…So that means Saber’s armor isn’t that strong against a Servant?”

残った手段は遠距離からの攻撃、魔術っていう飛び道具になる訳だけど、セイバーは騎士のクセにとんでもない対魔力を持ってるから、たいていの魔術は弾かれてしまうのよ」

pages.en:
“Right. But Saber herself is so skilled at close combat that hardly anyone could wound her in a melee.

“That leaves attacking from a distance—using magecraft as a projectile. Unfortunately, for a knight, Saber has outrageous Magic Resistance, so most magecraft simply bounces off her.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yeah. But Saber herself is skilled in combat, so it is pretty much impossible to hurt her in a hand-to-hand combat.
The remaining means would be attacking using magic from a distance, but since Saber has unbelievable magic resistance for a knight, she’ll repel most magic.”

pages.ja:
「不運に代表される呪いなんてまず届かないし、魔力を矢として放つ直接干渉も効かない。
セイバーを倒したかったら真っ正面からの斬り合いで、彼女を負かさなくちゃダメってワケ」

pages.en:
“Curses—the kind that inflict bad luck—almost never reach her, and directly interfering by firing magical energy like an arrow does not work either.

“If you want to defeat Saber, you have to face her head-on with a blade and beat her at her own game.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Curses like bad luck won’t touch her, and direct intervention like shooting an arrow of magical energy is useless.
So if one wishes to defeat Saber, one must fight her head on.”
“”

剣技で敵わないから魔術で勝負するっていうのに、魔術そのものがセイバーに効かないならどうしろっていうんだ。
なんか不公平だぞ、その話」

なんか不公平だぞ、その話」
pages.en:
“What? That's cheating.

“If you turn to magecraft because you can't beat her with a sword, but magecraft itself doesn't work on her, what are you supposed to do?

“There's something unfair about this whole arrangement.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey, that’s cheating.
They’re attacking with magic because they can’t beat her in combat, but if magic is useless against her, what are they supposed to do?
That’s really unfair.”

バーサーカーは力だけならセイバーを上回ってるし、ランサーだって白兵戦において必殺の槍を持ってる。
いま話しているライダーだってセイバーを出し抜くほどの宝具を持ってたんだから、セイバーも完璧ってワケじゃないわ」
pages.jaRuby:

いま話しているライダーだってセイバーを出し抜くほどの宝具を持ってたんだから、セイバーも完璧ってワケじゃないわ」
pages.en:
“Perhaps. But even Saber can't claim she'll never lose in close combat, can she?

“Berserker surpasses her in raw strength, and Lancer has a spear that kills without fail in a melee.

“Even Rider, whom we're discussing now, possessed a Noble Phantasm powerful enough to outmaneuver her. Saber is hardly invincible.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yup. But that doesn’t mean Saber can never be defeated in combat, right?
Berserker surpasses Saber in strength, and Lancer has his fatal lance in combat.
As we were just saying, Rider too has a Noble Phantasm that can even kill Saber, so it doesn’t mean Saber is perfect.”

pages.ja:
「わたしたちだってセイバーを倒す方法はあるもの。
単にセイバーの対魔力を上回る魔術を持ってくるか、サーヴァントが使ってる武器を借りて、寝ている間に首を切るとか。サーヴァントの武器ならサーヴァント自身と同じ霊格なんだから、傷を付ける事は可能なはずよ」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Even we have ways of defeating Saber.

“We could simply produce magecraft powerful enough to overcome her Magic Resistance. Or we could borrow a Servant's weapon and cut her throat in her sleep. A Servant's weapon possesses the same spiritual rank as its wielder, so it should be able to wound her.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“There are ways for even us to defeat Saber.
We just need to use magic that exceeds Saber’s magic resistance, or use the weapon she uses and cut her neck while she’s asleep. Servants’ weapons are in spirit form like them, so they should be able to hurt them.”

って、待て遠坂。

pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hmm.”
It’s a scary example, but I understand.
Hold on, Tohsaka.
You can’t talk like that in front of Saber herself.

pages.ja:
「そ、そうなんだ。
じゃあライダーの宝具が特別優れてるってワケじゃなくて、サーヴァントの攻撃だからセイバーも守りに徹したって事なのか」
pages.jaRuby:
「そ、そうなんだ。
じゃあライダーの宝具が特別優れてるってワケじゃなくて、サーヴァントの攻撃だからセイバーも守りに徹したって事なのか」
pages.en:
“R-right, I understand.

“Then Rider's Noble Phantasm wasn't unusually powerful. Saber only had to defend herself because another Servant was attacking her?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I-I see.
Then, it must be that Rider’s Noble Phantasm is not especially strong, but that Saber went into defense because it was an attack from a Servant?”

pages.ja:
「ワケないでしょ。セイバーが守りに徹するのなら、ライダー自身じゃ何をしたって追い詰める事なんて不可能よ。ライダー本人がそう優れた英霊じゃないのなら、彼女が宝具を使ったところでタカが知れているし。
そうでしょ、セイバー？ ライダーの宝具は、ライダー自身の能力とは“関係のない”武器なのよね？」

そうでしょ、セイバー？ ライダーの宝具は、ライダー自身の能力とは“関係のない”武器なのよね？」
pages.en:
“Of course not. If Saber devoted herself to defense, Rider herself could never corner her, no matter what she did. And if Rider isn't an especially distinguished Heroic Spirit, a Noble Phantasm drawing upon her own power would have definite limits.

“Isn't that right, Saber? Rider's Noble Phantasm was a weapon independent of Rider's own abilities.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Of course not. If Saber concentrated on defense, Rider herself couldn’t do anything to finish Saber. If Rider herself isn’t a superior heroic spirit, the Noble Phantasm she uses won’t be strong either.
Isn’t that right, Saber? Rider’s Noble Phantasm is unrelated to her ability, right?”

pages.ja:
「おそらく。ライダーの技や魔力に頼らない自動的な武装、宝具そのものに効果がある物だと思います。
魔術か幻想種か。
どちらにせよ、あの魔法陣から放たれたモノは圧倒的でした。直撃を受けた場合、生き延びられるサーヴァントなどいないでしょう」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:

pages.mirrorMoon:
“Probably. I believe it is an automatic weapon that does not rely on Rider’s skill or magical energy, or something that has an effect on the Noble Phantasm itself.
Magic or a fantastic race.
Either way, the thing released from that magic circle was overwhelming. I do not think any Servant would be able to survive if it received a direct blow.”

pages.mirrorMoon:
“Really? How is it, level-wise?”
“Putting it your way, I would say about an A+. It is just a speculation, so I cannot be certain.”

pages.ja:
「Ａ＋！？ なにそれ、魔法一歩手前じゃない……！
うわ、そんなの使われてよく学校が吹っ飛ばなかったってもんだわ」
pages.jaRuby:
「Ａ＋！？ なにそれ、魔法一歩手前じゃない……！
うわ、そんなの使われてよく学校が吹っ飛ばなかったってもんだわ」
pages.en:
“A+!? That's one step short of Magic…!

“Wow. It's a miracle the school was still standing after she used something like that.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“A+!? What is that!? That’s almost at the level of sorcery…!
Whoa, I’m surprised the school didn’t get blown away if something like that was used.”

pages.ja: 「単純に破壊するだけの宝具、という訳ではないのでしょう。元々は他の用途がある宝具なのではないでしょうか」
pages.jaRuby: 「単純に破壊するだけの宝具、という訳ではないのでしょう。元々は他の用途がある宝具なのではないでしょうか」
pages.en: “It may not be a Noble Phantasm intended merely for destruction. Perhaps it was originally created for some other purpose.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I believe it is not a Noble Phantasm that simply destroys. Perhaps it is a Noble Phantasm that has some other use.”

pages.ja: 「……そう。だとしても厄介ね。セイバーの話じゃＡ判定どころじゃないし、瞬間的な攻撃力ならサーヴァント中最高って事になるのかしら」
pages.jaRuby: 「……そう。だとしても厄介ね。セイバーの話じゃＡ判定どころじゃないし、瞬間的な攻撃力ならサーヴァント中最高って事になるのかしら」
pages.en: “…I see. Even so, that makes it troublesome. From your description, it goes well beyond an A rank. In terms of instantaneous destructive power, it might be the greatest among all the Servants.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…I see. But that’s a problem. According to Saber, it’s beyond an A rank, and her immediate attack power might be the strongest of all the Servants.”

pages.ja:
「………………ふん。まあ、確かに攻守共に優れた宝具のようでしたが……それより私の宝具の方が……」
ぼんやりと考え込む遠坂に、なんとも言えない顔つきで相づちをうつセイバー。
pages.jaRuby:
「………………ふん。まあ、確かに攻守共に優れた宝具のようでしたが……それより私の宝具の方が……」
ぼんやりと考え込む遠坂に、なんとも言えない顔つきで相づちをうつセイバー。
pages.en:
“…………Hmph. I admit that it appeared exceptional in both attack and defense… but my Noble Phantasm is——”

Saber answers the distracted Tohsaka with an expression I cannot quite interpret.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hmm. Well, it did seem like a Noble Phantasm superior in both attack and defense. …But my Noble Phantasm is more…”
Saber comments to Tohsaka, who goes into pondering.

pages.ja:
「……？」
なんだろう。
セイバー、なんか妙に面白くなさそうな様子だけど。
pages.jaRuby:
「……？」
なんだろう。
セイバー、なんか妙に面白くなさそうな様子だけど。
pages.en:
“…?”

What is it?

Saber looks strangely displeased.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…?”
What is it?
Saber doesn’t seem to be enjoying this conversation.

pages.ja:
「……セイバー？ 遠坂の意見、何かひっかかるところでもあるのか？」
「え……？ あ、いえ、別にそういう訳ではないと言うか……ええ、本当はどちらが強いかなど、追究するのは騎士にあるまじき行いというか……」
pages.jaRuby:
「……セイバー？ 遠坂の意見、何かひっかかるところでもあるのか？」
「え……？ あ、いえ、別にそういう訳ではないと言うか……ええ、本当はどちらが強いかなど、追究するのは騎士にあるまじき行いというか……」
pages.en:
“…Saber? Is there something about Tohsaka's opinion that bothers you?”

“What…? Ah, no. It isn't precisely that… Indeed, debating which of us is stronger would be conduct unworthy of a knight…”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Saber? Is something Tohsaka said worrying you?”
“Eh…? Um, no, that is not correct… yes, I believe it is inappropriate for a knight to inquire into who is the strongest…”

pages.ja:
「？」
挙動不審。
セイバーは自分の態度を恥じるように、ごにょごにょと言葉を濁す。
pages.jaRuby:
「？」
挙動不審。
セイバーは自分の態度を恥じるように、ごにょごにょと言葉を濁す。
pages.en:
“?”

She is behaving very strangely.

As if ashamed of herself, Saber mumbles the rest beneath her breath.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…?”
She’s acting suspiciously.
Saber mumbles on as if ashamed of what she’s saying.

pages.ja: 「……まあいいけど。それよりさ、さっき妙なコトを言ってなかったか？ セイバーとランサーのは対人宝具とかなんとか」
pages.jaRuby: 「……まあいいけど。それよりさ、さっき妙なコトを言ってなかったか？ セイバーとランサーのは対人宝具とかなんとか」
pages.en: “…Well, never mind. More importantly, didn't you say something odd a moment ago? Something about yours and Lancer's being Anti-Unit Noble Phantasms?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Oh well. But weren’t you saying something weird earlier? Something about your and Lancer’s weapons being anti-personnel Noble Phantasms?”

pages.ja:
「対人宝具、ですか……？ いえ、言葉通りの意味ですが。私の風王結界やランサーのゲイボルクは、あくまで“人を倒す”為の武装です。
いかに強力な魔力、呪いを帯びていたところで、その用途は対人の域を出るモノではありません」
pages.jaRuby:
「対人宝具、ですか……？ いえ、言葉通りの意味ですが。私の風王結界やランサーのゲイボルクは、あくまで“人を倒す”為の武装です。
いかに強力な魔力、呪いを帯びていたところで、その用途は対人の域を出るモノではありません」
pages.en:
“Anti-Unit Noble Phantasms…? The term means precisely what it suggests. My Invisible Air and Lancer's Gae Bolg are armaments intended to defeat an individual.

“However powerful the magical energy or curse they bear, their purpose does not extend beyond combat against a single person.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Anti-personnel Noble Phantasm…? It means what it says. My ‘Invisible Air’ and Lancer’s Gae Bolg are only weapons to defeat people.
No matter how strong the magical energy or curse it wields, it does not go beyond the level of defeating other beings.”

pages.ja:
……まあ、それはその通りか。
刀身が見えないセイバーの剣は、確かに戦いにおいて有利だ。
pages.jaRuby:
……まあ、それはその通りか。
刀身が見えないセイバーの剣は、確かに戦いにおいて有利だ。
pages.en:
…That much does make sense.

The invisibility of Saber's blade certainly gives her an advantage in battle.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Well, that is true.
Saber’s invisible sword is certainly an advantage in battle.

pages.ja:
だがそれはあくまで人対人に限る。
薪をたくさん割ろうという時、剣が見えようと見えまいと割るスピードに変化はないだろう。
ランサーのゲイボルクも同様だ。
必ず心臓を貫く、という呪いの槍とて、相手が岩や家ならただの頑丈な槍にすぎない。
pages.jaRuby:
だがそれはあくまで人対人に限る。
薪をたくさん割ろうという時、剣が見えようと見えまいと割るスピードに変化はないだろう。
ランサーのゲイボルクも同様だ。
必ず心臓を貫く、という呪いの槍とて、相手が岩や家ならただの頑丈な槍にすぎない。
pages.en:
But only in a contest between one person and another.

If she wanted to split a great heap of firewood, whether the blade was visible would make no difference to the speed of the work.

The same applies to Lancer's Gae Bolg.

Even a cursed spear guaranteed to pierce the heart becomes nothing more than an unusually sturdy spear when its target is a rock or a house.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But that is only in the case of man versus man.
There would be no difference in speed, even if you used an invisible sword to chop wood.
Lancer’s Gae Bolg is the same.
Even with a cursed lance that will strike the heart, if the opponent is a rock or a house, it is no more than a strong lance.

pages.ja:
「……なるほど、だから対人の宝具って事なのか。
ならライダーの宝具は
」
pages.jaRuby:
「……なるほど、だから対人の宝具って事なのか。
ならライダーの宝具は
」
pages.en:
“…I see. That's why they're called Anti-Unit Noble Phantasms.

“Then Rider's must be——”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I see, so that’s why it’s an anti-personnel Noble Phantasm.
Then Rider’s Noble Phantasm is”

pages.ja: 「対軍宝具って事になるわね。そう言えば父さんに聞いた事があったわ。宝具には対人に優れたもの、対軍に優れたものがあるって」
pages.jaRuby: 「対軍宝具って事になるわね。そう言えば父さんに聞いた事があったわ。宝具には対人に優れたもの、対軍に優れたものがあるって」
pages.en: “An Anti-Army Noble Phantasm. Come to think of it, my father once told me that some Noble Phantasms excel against individuals, while others excel against armies.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I would say that it’s an anti-army Noble Phantasm. Come to think of it, I heard from my father that there are Noble Phantasms specialized against others, and Noble Phantasms specialized against armies.”

pages.ja:
「簡単に言って、対人宝具は弾数制限のない拳銃で、対軍宝具ってのは一発かぎりのミサイルって事ね。
ライダーの宝具は強力だけど、その分使用にかなりの制限があるんじゃないかしら。少なくとも、セイバーの剣みたいに“いつも視えない”なんて永続的な宝具じゃない」
pages.jaRuby:
「簡単に言って、対人宝具は弾数制限のない拳銃で、対軍宝具ってのは一発かぎりのミサイルって事ね。
ライダーの宝具は強力だけど、その分使用にかなりの制限があるんじゃないかしら。少なくとも、セイバーの剣みたいに“いつも視えない”なんて永続的な宝具じゃない」
pages.en:
“Put simply, an Anti-Unit Noble Phantasm is a handgun with unlimited ammunition, while an Anti-Army Noble Phantasm is a missile you can fire only once.

“Rider's Noble Phantasm may be powerful, but I imagine that power comes with severe restrictions on its use. At the very least, it isn't permanently active the way Saber's sword is ‘always invisible.’”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“To put it simply, the anti-personnel Noble Phantasms are guns with unlimited ammo, and the anti-army Noble Phantasms are one-time missiles.
Rider’s Noble Phantasm is powerful, but it’s not a continuous Noble Phantasm like Saber’s sword, which is always invisible.”

pages.ja:
「な
」
ちょっと待て。
拳銃とミサイルなんて、そんなのは勝負にならない。
そりゃあセイバーの“視えない剣”だって凄い剣だけど、そんなデタラメな宝具の前じゃ剣を振るう前に吹き飛ばされる
pages.jaRuby:
「な
」

そりゃあセイバーの“視えない剣”だって凄い剣だけど、そんなデタラメな宝具の前じゃ剣を振るう前に吹き飛ばされる
pages.en:
“Wha——”

Wait a minute.

A handgun against a missile is no contest at all.

Saber's invisible sword may be remarkable, but against an absurd Noble Phantasm like that, she would be blown away before she could even swing it——
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wha”
Hold on.
A gun would be no match for a missile.
It’s true that Saber’s invisible sword is an awesome sword, but it’ll be blown away before she could swing it against such a ridiculous Noble Phantasm

pages.ja: 「……つまり。ライダーと戦うのなら、宝具を使われる前に倒せってコトか」
pages.jaRuby: 「……つまり。ライダーと戦うのなら、宝具を使われる前に倒せってコトか」
pages.en: “…In other words, if we fight Rider, we have to defeat her before she uses her Noble Phantasm.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…So in short, if we’re going to fight her, you’re saying we should defeat Rider before she uses her Noble Phantasm?”

pages.ja:
「でしょうね。宝具の打ち合いになったら勝ち目はない。
ライダーと慎二を捜すっていうんなら、それだけは頭に入れておきなさい。
大前提として、ライダーが宝具を使う前に倒すコト。
戦いを長引かせれば長引かせるだけこっちが不利になるから」
pages.jaRuby:
「でしょうね。宝具の打ち合いになったら勝ち目はない。
ライダーと慎二を捜すっていうんなら、それだけは頭に入れておきなさい。
大前提として、ライダーが宝具を使う前に倒すコト。
戦いを長引かせれば長引かせるだけこっちが不利になるから」
pages.en:
“Exactly. If it comes down to an exchange of Noble Phantasms, you have no chance of winning.

“If you intend to search for Rider and Shinji, remember that above all else.

“The absolute condition is that you defeat Rider before she can use her Noble Phantasm.

“The longer the battle continues, the worse your position becomes.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I would think so. You’ll have no chance of winning if it comes down to the Noble Phantasm.
Remember if you’re going to go look for Shinji and Rider,
the biggest requirement is to defeat Rider before she has a chance to use her Noble Phantasm.
It’ll be to your disadvantage if you let the fight last longer.”

pages.ja: 「もしくは私が戦っている間にライダーのマスターを倒せばいい。あのマスターに戦闘手段はないのだから、そちらの方が確実かもしれません」
pages.jaRuby: 「もしくは私が戦っている間にライダーのマスターを倒せばいい。あのマスターに戦闘手段はないのだから、そちらの方が確実かもしれません」
pages.en: “Alternatively, Shirou could defeat Rider's Master while I occupy her. That Master has no means of fighting for himself, so it may be the more reliable course.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Or you can just defeat Rider’s Master while I am fighting. He has no means of fighting, so that might be more certain.”

pages.ja:
それが結論だ。
対抗策がない以上、使われる前に倒すしかない。
他のサーヴァントの宝具がなんであれ、ライダーとだけは宝具の競い合いをしてはいけない、という事か。
pages.jaRuby:
それが結論だ。
対抗策がない以上、使われる前に倒すしかない。
他のサーヴァントの宝具がなんであれ、ライダーとだけは宝具の競い合いをしてはいけない、という事か。
pages.en:
That settles it.

Without any means of countering Rider's Noble Phantasm, we have no choice but to defeat her before she can use it.

Whatever Noble Phantasms the other Servants may possess, Rider is the one opponent we must never challenge to a contest of trump cards.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s the conclusion.
We don’t know what Rider’s Noble Phantasm is, and additionally, it is too powerful.
As we have no countermeasure, we can only beat her before she has a chance to use it.
So whatever the Noble Phantasms of the other Servants are, we cannot compete in Noble Phantasms against Rider.

「……忠告助かったよ、遠坂。
俺たちは慎二を捜しに行くけど、遠坂はどうする。留守番していてくれるか？」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Thanks for the warning, Tohsaka.

“We're going to look for Shinji. What will you do? Would you mind staying here?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Your advice was helpful, Tohsaka.
We’ll be going to go look for Shinji, but what about you? Will you stay here?”

pages.ja:
「……そうね、貴方たちがそう言うなら、わたしたちも慎二を捜してもいいんだけど
ま、止めとくわ。
敵はライダーだけじゃないし、わたしたちは元々バーサーカーを倒す為に手を組んだんだしね。
士郎が慎二を追っている間、わたしはわたしでやる事があるから」
pages.jaRuby:
「……そうね、貴方たちがそう言うなら、わたしたちも慎二を捜してもいいんだけど

pages.en:
“…Well, if the two of you insist, we could help search for Shinji too—but no. I think I'll pass.

“Rider isn't our only enemy, and we originally joined forces to defeat Berserker.

“While you're chasing Shinji, I have work of my own to do.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Yeah, if you say so, we can go look for Shinji as wellbut I guess we won’t.
Rider isn’t our only enemy. And we originally cooperated to fight against Berserker.
I have something I need to do as well while you guys are looking for Shinji.”

pages.ja:
どこか冷たい笑みをこぼして、遠坂は席を立つ。
「それじゃあね。いい結果を期待しているわ」
pages.jaRuby:

Tohsaka rises from her seat with a cold little smile.

“Goodbye, then. I look forward to hearing the results.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka stands up with a cold smile on her face.
“See you. I’ll be expecting good results.”
